title: Zhaozhou Bridge
summary: The Zhaozhou Bridge is a single-arch stone bridge in Zhao County, Hebei, designed and built in the Sui dynasty by the stonemason Li Chun. ASCE records its completion as 605 and calls it the world's oldest open-spandrel arch bridge. Its main arch spans about 37 m, and the bridge has been repaired several times, most thoroughly in the mid-1950s.

uncertainty.note: Completion in 605 is from ASCE; China Daily says built around 605. A 2026 scholarly paper dates it to 581-600, so the start range allows 24 years earlier. End is the present: the bridge stands.
